_meta.description: Field mappings for the orders service log stream. Applied by scripts/elk_init.sh before Logstash writes its first document — a mapping created AFTER data exists cannot be changed without reindexing.
_meta.note_on_message: message is text (full-text search) PLUS a keyword subfield (aggregation). That pair is Elasticsearch's default for strings, and the dynamic_template above switches it off everywhere else deliberately: a keyword subfield on trace_id is pure waste, because you filter by a trace ID, you never group by one. slog messages are the opposite — static, low-cardinality strings — and 'which message is flooding my index?' is the first question asked when the bill jumps. Keep the subfield exactly where you aggregate.
_meta.note_on_comments: Arbitrary keys belong HERE, not in properties. Anything added under properties is parsed as a FIELD MAPPING, and a string there fails the whole template with 'Expected map for property [fields]'.
